units.text: # Lilly's July 1645 sickness enquiry: historical-source audit
12 October 2026 · B02p · William Lilly, *Christian Astrology* (1647), Chapter XLVI
## Scope and evidence class

Chapter **XLVI**, headed *Whether the Sick would live or dye, and what his Disease was?*, begins on original PDF323 / printed289 with a dated horoscope and continues through the complete illness judgment and author-reported death on PDF324 / printed290 **above** the separator introducing Chapter XLVII. The two admitted pages contain **one question, one chart, one patient as reported by Lilly, and one author-reported outcome**. They do not contain 24 independently observed cases. [Original PDF323–324; SECTION_COVERAGE.json; CASE_EVIDENCE.json]

This candidate has **24 reference-only documentary records R1770–R1793**, including chart labeling, parts of Lilly's explanation, prognosis, reported outcome, retrospective transits, ONE editorial derived-arithmetic record (R1789), and ONE editorial boundary record (R1793). If source-review accepted and integrated, the 1,769 previously retained Lilly records would become **1,793**, and with 1,066 retained Ptolemy records the combined inventory would be **2,859**. These are textual rule/inference units, not empirical astrology successes. [RULES.json; COUNTS.json; retained cumulative index]
## Chart inscription and calendar

The centre reads **Die Mercurij, 16 Julij 1645, 7:22 AM:, hor: ♄**, identifying a *Wednesday* query date and a **separate** Saturn planetary-hour designation (visually an h-shaped sign, medium-high-confidence Saturn identification). A contextual reading in English 1645 is **16 July Julian** (equivalent to 26 July on the extended/proleptic Gregorian calendar, also a Wednesday), but the image does not explicitly label the calendar, location or time zone. The original wheel is not an independently verified ephemeris. Provisional cusp labels and uncertain planet glyphs are logged separately in CHART_INSCRIPTION.json. The lunar and planetary placements must not be transformed into modern timing rules without a separate source-qualified calculation. [PDF323; CHART_INSCRIPTION.json; U02–U05]

This is a **different dated enquiry and chart** from the previously accepted Chapter XLV sick-doctor figure dated 8 May 1645. These are distinct questions and charts; the passages do not determine whether the two patients are identical or different. Chapter XLV's previously mistaken May24 caption was corrected using **the B02o source images and correction record**, not from the present PDF323; the July16 chart neither supersedes nor explains that earlier case. [B02o/CHAPTER_XLV_DATE_CORRECTION.md; B02o/CHART_INSCRIPTION.json; R1771; U21]
## What the author attributes to celestial conditions

At the outset, **Virgo rising** is described as **most afflicted** by the **corporeal presence of Mars**, which the author also partly associates with the eighth-house rulership. For disease location and causes he considers the sixth-house **Aquarius**, the sixth ruler **Saturn in Taurus** (described as fixed, earthy, melancholic and of Virgo's triplicity), and the **Moon near Mars in the ascendant**. The additional glyph afflicting Aquarius is legible as a Dragon-tail form **☋**, with exact ☋/☊ orientation retained as a copy-specific uncertainty. [PDF323 continuing on PDF324; R1773–R1777; U05–U06,U10]

From these testimonies the author infers spleen problems, wind-colic, melancholy bowel obstructions, small fevers, a 'remisse Pulse', head disturbance and restless sleep, with an open '&c.' in the original. The next bracketed claim, **“All which was true”**, is **Lilly's own retrospective corroboration**. This is not an independently documented examination, another patient, or an objective confirmation of the historical horoscope's accuracy. Modern diagnoses are outside the source-audit contract. [PDF324/printed290; R1778–R1781; U12–U13]
## The unusual ten-or-twelve-day account

Lilly says he encouraged the patient to put his affairs in order and make peace with God, stating he could not perceive natural grounds for living longer than **ten or twelve days**. That statement is followed by four rationales: the Sun's asserted perfect square to Saturn as sixth ruler, **both in fixed signs**; Mars physically at the ascendant, naturally adverse and **accidentally almost** ruler of the eighth; the Moon near **Cauda Leonis** and afflicted by Mars; and a lunar separation from Mercury's sextile, judged **more properly a square in signs of long ascensions**, followed by virtue transferred to Jupiter as eighth lord (Mercury is the ascendant ruler, and the antecedent of 'his vertue' remains unresolved). All four are preserved with their named conditions and original-terminology uncertainties; they are not four independent patient outcomes. [PDF324; R1782–R1787; U07–U11]

The text then reports that the patient **'dyed' on the provisionally read 28 July following** (the first date digit is weakly printed; 'died' is modernized wording). The qualified July28 reading minus July16 is **12 days by exclusive subtraction**, which matches the upper number only if the earlier warning was timed from the question date; the text does not supply that start moment. This is a real arithmetic correspondence *within the printed account*. Crucially, both the prediction and the outcome appear in a book printed in 1647 describing events in 1645. No independent death record, pre-outcome manuscript, timestamped prediction freeze or denominator of missed cases has been established. It therefore cannot be counted as a validated prospective forecast of exactly 12 days. [PDF323–324; R1783,R1788–R1789; CASE_EVIDENCE.json; U14–U16]

The remaining passage says Mercury came to the **question-figure Sun's degree** and 'therein' squared Saturn; this is separate from Lilly's earlier Sun–Saturn rationale. It then says the Moon opposed the Sun, and the Moon **'that day'** transited the sixth cusp; the referent of 'that day' (reported July28 or preceding day) is unresolved. These Mercury/Sun/Saturn and Moon/Sun/cusp descriptions occur **after the death statement**. They are presented as retrospective explanatory transits, not as original pre-frozen targets. The final degrees and aspect calculations have not been reproduced against verified historical ephemerides or an independently implemented house system. [PDF324; R1790–R1792; U17–U18]
## Witness fidelity and limits

The original source is the 894-page Wellcome 1647 scan of *Christian Astrology* (SHA-256 `2cb53e20e122ffc6e47917ba10241f6c49687cd7a4696f3b5db655a2a1aab28b`). This contribution preserves two source images and the original volume's own printed errata page as a same-volume correction register. Original printed claims are distinct from the normalized source-record paraphrases, contemporary calculations, and editorial cautions. The original errata page was inspected for corrections affecting printed289–290; no entry for printed page289 or290 appears in that selective errata list; absence is not proof of faultless wording. [SOURCE_IDENTITY.json; SOURCE_IMAGE_MANIFEST.json; SOURCE_FIRST_NOTES.md; UNRESOLVED.json]

The unresolved ledger retains **40 explicit issues**: glyph identity, calendar and clock frame, early-modern body/planetary meanings, translation-of-light and aspect conventions, the identity of **Cauda Leonis**, author-reported outcome credibility and the absence of independent predictive or medical tests. All proposed rules remain **REFERENCE_ONLY_NOT_PROMOTED**. These source claims are not medical advice or a deployed birth/life-timing model. [UNRESOLVED.json; RULES.json]
## Independent 1647 source-reader corrections

The independent reader examined **both admitted Chapter XLVI original pages**, not five pages. It read both body pages, the original chart wheel and the same-volume errata. The strongest fault in the first draft was the after-death lunar cusp statement. The original PDF324/printed290 says the Moon transited the degree of the **sixth house, viz. 14 of Aquarius**, not a first-house Virgo cusp. The revised R1792 keeps the body reading, with the wheel's approximately **13°32′ Aquarius** label separately preserved; an ordinal-fourteenth-degree or rounding *interpretation* is possible, but neither equivalence is printed or proven. The Sun-twelfth-cusp continuation stays an elliptical retrospective clause. [PDF323–324; R1792; CHART_INSCRIPTION.json; U18,U32]

The source page describes the sixth-house Aquarius as afflicted by a node-like **☋** (exact orientation still source-qualified), and separately names the Moon near **Cauda Leonis**. These are not silently equated. The Moon is described as afflicted **by Mars**, not the reverse; a printed adverse influence does not by itself prove an additional square. [PDF323–324; R1775,R1786; U05,U07,U28]

The wheel has provisional house-cusp labels and a provisional glyph/adjacent-numerals table; most planet signs, including Venus/Mercury associations, remain unresolved. Original print spells the clock **7:22 AM:**, not a modernized exact quotation “7:22 A.M.”. The chart's original date is given as Wednesday 16 July 1645; the Julian inference is grounded in its historical English weekday but the printed h-shaped Saturn planetary-hour glyph, modern time standard, UTC offset, location and external ephemeris have not all been independently established. [PDF323; CHART_INSCRIPTION.json]

The Latin vital-principle phrase and **both bodies in fixed signs** in the first prognostic reason have been restored. The fourth reason prints lunar transfer of **“his vertue”**; its referent is most plausibly Mercury but not explicitly resolved. The source says its significators promised no less than death, but supplies no computation for the **ten or twelve days**. Subsequent claimed transits occur in the narrative only **after** the death report. [PDF324; R1784,R1787,R1789–R1792; CASE_EVIDENCE.json; UNRESOLVED.json]

An original heading within the first page reads **“Judgment of the Figure aforesaid.”** The original's handwritten 6th House margin note and ruled annotations are not established as authorial. No horoscope, diagnosis, outcome or calendar result in this chapter has been cross-validated against a real patient's records; the text supplies one retrospective author narrative only. [PDF323–324; SECTION_COVERAGE.json; CASE_EVIDENCE.json]
## Exact next boundary

After the death and retrospective transit paragraph on PDF324 / printed290, a horizontal divider introduces **Chapter XLVII — Of the CRYSIS in Diseases**. The new chapter starts **below** that divider and continues onto PDF325 onward. It is not included in this one-case packet. The parent Lilly and multi-author source study remains **OPEN**. The next record after an accepted R1793 would be **R1794**, subject to checking the live cumulative index before assigning it. [PDF324–325; SECTION_COVERAGE.json; CONTINUE_HANDOFF.md]
